html:
Swabia is a region of southwestern Germany, and in 1800 it was a patchwork of small states inside the Holy Roman Empire, grouped together as the Swabian Circle. The name goes back to the Suebi and Alemanni and to the medieval Duchy of Swabia, which fell apart after the Hohenstaufen dynasty died out in the 13th century.

What remained was a crowd of small lordships: the Duchy of Württemberg, the margraves of Baden, abbeys, counts, imperial knights and dozens of free imperial cities such as Ulm and Augsburg. The Swabian Circle, set up around 1500, let them keep the peace, share military duties and run roads and coinage together.

Napoleon swept this away. Between 1803 and 1806 the church lands and most free cities were handed to the bigger states. Württemberg became a kingdom and Baden a grand duchy, both in the Confederation of the Rhine, and the Empire itself ended in 1806.
